key_insight: Machine learning on electronic health records can surface hidden prediagnostic patterns for several rare genetic diseases, sometimes years before a formal diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help clinicians prioritize patients for review and confirmatory genetic testing earlier in the diagnostic journey.
method: Trained ML models on billing codes plus phenotypes extracted from clinical notes.
Applied the models to a longitudinal Mayo Clinic EHR cohort of about 3 million patient records.
Tested performance across eight rare conditions using a high-specificity setting.
evidence_signal: Across eight conditions, early identification ranged from 10% to 89% at 99% specificity, with median lead times often exceeding one year before the first diagnostic billing code.
watch_item: Performance varied widely by condition, so real-world use will need careful validation to avoid missed cases and workflow burden.
paper_title: Early identification of rare disease using deep phenotyping of electronic health records
